### What does this PR do?

The `rollout.n` samples of a GRPO prompt share that prompt, but the actor, ref and critic forwards compute it `n` times. With `fsdp_config.use_prefix_packing=True`, we pack adjacent samples with an identical prompt as one trunk plus one branch per sample, so we compute the prompt once:

```
before: [prompt | resp_1] [prompt | resp_2] ... [prompt | resp_n]
after:  [prompt[:-1]] [prompt[-1] | resp_1] ... [prompt[-1] | resp_n]
```

| segment | queries | keys |
|---|---|---|
| trunk | `prompt[:-1]` | `prompt[:-1]` |
| branch i | `prompt[-1] + resp_i` | `prompt[:-1] + prompt[-1] + resp_i` |

We gather keys and values after RoPE, so a branch never sees another branch, and bottom-right causal alignment gives each branch token the full trunk plus its own earlier tokens, as in the unpacked sequence. In backward, the gather sums the branches' gradients on the trunk keys onto the trunk, which is the unpacked gradient. We pass `cu_seqlens` explicitly because branch positions do not restart at 0, so boundaries derived from `position_ids` would merge the branches.

This is one varlen flash-attention call per layer, the same call the rmpad path already makes: no new kernel, mask or dependency. Each branch starts with a copy of the last prompt token, because `no_padding_2_padding` reads the first response log-prob from that row; with it, the rolled labels, fused kernels, entropy, Σπ² and the critic work unchanged. We map outputs back with one `index_select` per tensor, so nothing below the model forward changes. A per-micro-batch counter raises if any attention layer bypasses the packed wrapper, so an unsupported model fails loudly instead of letting branches attend to each other. Off by default; without the flag, users run today's code.

GRPO on Qwen3-4B, `rollout.n=8`, 2x H100: a training step is **2.7x faster** with a 2k-token prompt and 1.18x faster on plain GSM8K (83-token prompts), with reward curves matching within sampling noise. Peak memory is unchanged in those runs; in a single-GPU forward+backward sweep the speedup reaches 3.8x at an 8k prompt and peak memory halves (35.8 → 18.7 GB).

RFC: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/issues/8299. Related: #6401 / #6689 (prefix-tree attention for Megatron with MAGI/Flex; FSDP listed as planned); #4368 (PrefixGrouper: forked the old `dp_actor.py` forward and needed `use_remove_padding=False`, no caller since #6067); #7202 (tried to revive that fork, closed in favour of #6689; this PR sits in the engine on the rmpad path instead); #7561 (Megatron RFC).

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+prefix+packing+OR+%22prefix+grouper%22+OR+%22prefix+tree%22 . Not a duplicate: #6689 covers the Megatron engine and needs MAGI or FlexAttention; this PR changes the FSDP engine, uses the flash-attention varlen path it already runs, and overlaps with #6689 only in shared glue (`ray_trainer.py`, `trainer_base.py`, `workers/engine/utils.py`, `workers/config/engine.py` and its generated yaml), not in any attention or engine code.
- [x] Title format `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`

### Test

We test packed-equals-unpacked by two independent routes, so the oracle and the production path do not share an attention implementation.

CPU, exact (`cpu_unit_tests.yml` picks up the `_on_cpu.py` files; the two `tests/utils` files run in `gpu_unit_tests.yml`):
```bash
pytest tests/workers/test_prefix_packing_on_cpu.py tests/workers/test_prefix_packing_engine_on_cpu.py \
  tests/utils/test_prepare_micro_batches_with_group_size.py tests/utils/test_seqlen_balancing.py
```
We run a tiny fp32 Qwen2 through SDPA with a hand-built dense tree mask, which we first check against a brute-force per-sample forward, and require packed log-probs, entropy, values and every parameter gradient to match at `atol=1e-5`. We also unit-test pack/unpack round trips, label alignment, group-detection edge cases, tail padding, the nothing-shared fallback, every rejection check, the layer guard (including across FSDP's kwarg copy) and micro-batch grouping.

GPU (added to `model.yml` next to `test_transformer.py`), H100, flash-attn 2.8.3, transformers 5.12.1:
```bash
pytest -s tests/models/test_prefix_packing.py   # 14 passed
```
We compare the production path (bf16, varlen flash-attention, the packed wrapper) against the existing rmpad forward: Qwen2 (with and without sliding window) and Qwen3, fused kernels on/off, gradient checkpointing on/off, plus the critic, plus an sdpa model that must leave the layer counter at zero. Log-probs and entropy match within `atol=1e-2`, gradient cosine > 0.999.

End-to-end GRPO, Qwen3-4B, 2x H100, FSDP + vLLM, `rollout.n=8`, 128 prompts/step, 20 steps, mean of steps 5-20, the flag the only difference:

| | 2k-token prompt: baseline | packed | speedup | GSM8K (83-token prompt): baseline | packed | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `timing_s/old_log_prob` | 44.8 s | 14.3 s | 3.13x | 15.8 s | 13.3 s | 1.19x |
| `timing_s/ref` | 60.5 s | 15.6 s | 3.88x | 17.1 s | 11.1 s | 1.54x |
| `timing_s/update_actor` | 158.4 s | 51.2 s | 3.09x | 69.2 s | 59.3 s | 1.17x |
| `timing_s/step` | 289.5 s | 107.1 s | **2.70x** | 123.0 s | 104.4 s | **1.18x** |
| `prefix_packing_token_ratio` | | 3.65 | | | 1.10 | |

With the long prompt the actor phases reach ~85% of the 3.65x token saving and the ref exceeds it. On GSM8K every phase beats the 1.10x token saving (1.18x on the step), because dynamic batching now budgets by packed length and runs fewer, fuller micro-batches; the token ratio is a floor on the speedup, not an estimate of it. Rewards match within sampling noise (per-step difference mean -0.003, sd 0.009 with the long prompt; +0.010, sd 0.013 on GSM8K; the binomial standard error of a 1024-sample mean is ~0.01). Peak allocated memory is 38.25 GB per GPU in all four runs, so at this batch size a fixed floor sets the peak and packing neither raises nor lowers it.

Single-GPU forward+backward sweep (Qwen3-4B, fused kernels, gradient checkpointing, 8 x 1024 response tokens): speedup 1.06x at a 64-token prompt, 2.18x at 2048, 3.81x at 8192, at least 84% of the token ratio throughout; peak memory never rises and falls from 35.8 to 18.7 GB at 8192, so the same GPU holds roughly twice the response tokens per micro-batch.

### API and Usage Example

```bash
actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.use_prefix_packing=True   # ref follows the actor
critic.fsdp.use_prefix_packing=True
```
Off by default; a user who does not set it runs today's code. If the dead `use_prefix_grouper` flag is also set, prefix packing wins (`balance_batch` follows the packing grouping); we remove that flag in a follow-up. We check at model build that `use_remove_padding=True`, `ulysses_sequence_parallel_size=1`, `flash_attention_2`/`3` on CUDA with flash-attn >= 2.1, a text-only model, and not a model that takes `cu_seqlens` directly (linear-attention hybrids), and we reject top-k distillation, score centering, router replay and multi-modal inputs per micro-batch, each with an explicit error.

### Design & Code Changes

- `verl/workers/utils/prefix_packing.py` (new): group detection by prompt token ids (exact by construction, no `uid` needed), the pack/unpack plan, budget helpers, the support checks and the layer counter.
- `verl/workers/engine/fsdp/transformer_impl.py`: pack in `prepare_model_inputs`, unpack in `prepare_model_outputs` (actor and critic); run plain rmpad when a micro-batch shares nothing; raise if any attention layer bypassed the packed path; log `prefix_packing_token_ratio`.
- `verl/models/transformers/monkey_patch.py`, `dense_common.py`: the flash-attention wrapper handles the `prefix_packing` kwarg (gather K/V, explicit `cu_seqlens`, record the layer); the fused-kernel forward passes it on.
- `verl/utils/seqlen_balancing.py`, `verl/workers/engine/utils.py`: dynamic batching keeps same-prompt samples in one micro-batch, budgeted by packed length, and splits a group over budget with its own trunk per part.
- `verl/trainer/ppo/ray_trainer.py`, `v1/trainer_base.py`, `trainer/ppo/utils.py`: with the flag on, `balance_batch` keeps each prompt's samples on one rank.
- `verl/workers/utils/padding.py`: `get_prompt_lens` shared with the packer.
- Config field (`workers/config/engine.py`, yaml), docs (`docs/perf/perf_tuning.rst`, `docs/examples/config.rst`), example toggle in `run_qwen3_4b_fsdp.sh`, CI step in `model.yml`.

Follow-ups, not in this PR: linear-attention hybrids (recurrent-state handoff at the trunk inside the existing `qwen3_5.py` packed-sequence patch), Ulysses SP, sharing beyond the prompt for multi-turn trees, removing the dead PrefixGrouper code.

I developed this PR myself and used AI assistance for code review, test design and this write-up. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

- [x] Docs updated.
- [x] Tests added to CI.
- [x] CI requested in the `ci-request` Slack channel.

Fixed in d6dfcb28. The failure was reachable: balance_batch equalises samples per rank, not groups, so once a rank splits an over-budget group (or merges two identical prompts), ranks can hold different group counts, and the agreed micro-batch count can exceed a rank’s group count.

The only missing piece was that a rank with too few groups raised instead of making more. So rearrange_micro_batches now takes group_trunk_lens, and inside that loop, whenever the agreed count exceeds this rank’s group count, it splits the largest group in two, each part keeping its own trunk, until it has enough. A part is never longer than its parent, so it still fits the budget, and the split is local, so no new collectives. This runs on the initial MAX and again on every later raise of the count. Forced groups (force_group_size) can’t be split and keep the old error.

+Shared-prefix packing (FSDP)

detail.body:
### What does this PR do?

The `rollout.n` samples of a GRPO prompt share that prompt, but the actor, ref and critic forwards compute it `n` times. With `fsdp_config.use_prefix_packing=True`, we pack adjacent samples with an identical prompt as one trunk plus one branch per sample, so we compute the prompt once:

```
before: [prompt | resp_1] [prompt | resp_2] ... [prompt | resp_n]
after:  [prompt[:-1]] [prompt[-1] | resp_1] ... [prompt[-1] | resp_n]
```

| segment | queries | keys |
|---|---|---|
| trunk | `prompt[:-1]` | `prompt[:-1]` |
| branch i | `prompt[-1] + resp_i` | `prompt[:-1] + prompt[-1] + resp_i` |

We gather keys and values after RoPE, so a branch never sees another branch, and bottom-right causal alignment gives each branch token the full trunk plus its own earlier tokens, as in the unpacked sequence. In backward, the gather sums the branches' gradients on the trunk keys onto the trunk, which is the unpacked gradient. We pass `cu_seqlens` explicitly because branch positions do not restart at 0, so boundaries derived from `position_ids` would merge the branches.

This is one varlen flash-attention call per layer, the same call the rmpad path already makes: no new kernel, mask or dependency. Each branch starts with a copy of the last prompt token, because `no_padding_2_padding` reads the first response log-prob from that row; with it, the rolled labels, fused kernels, entropy, Σπ² and the critic work unchanged. We map outputs back with one `index_select` per tensor, so nothing below the model forward changes. A per-micro-batch counter raises if any attention layer bypasses the packed wrapper, so an unsupported model fails loudly instead of letting branches attend to each other. Off by default; without the flag, users run today's code.

GRPO on Qwen3-4B, `rollout.n=8`, 2x H100: a training step is **2.7x faster** with a 2k-token prompt and 1.18x faster on plain GSM8K (83-token prompts), with reward curves matching within sampling noise. Peak memory is unchanged in those runs; in a single-GPU forward+backward sweep the speedup reaches 3.8x at an 8k prompt and peak memory halves (35.8 → 18.7 GB).

RFC: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/issues/8299. Related: #6401 / #6689 (prefix-tree attention for Megatron with MAGI/Flex; FSDP listed as planned); #4368 (PrefixGrouper: forked the old `dp_actor.py` forward and needed `use_remove_padding=False`, no caller since #6067); #7202 (tried to revive that fork, closed in favour of #6689; this PR sits in the engine on the rmpad path instead); #7561 (Megatron RFC).

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+prefix+packing+OR+%22prefix+grouper%22+OR+%22prefix+tree%22 . Not a duplicate: #6689 covers the Megatron engine and needs MAGI or FlexAttention; this PR changes the FSDP engine, uses the flash-attention varlen path it already runs, and overlaps with #6689 only in shared glue (`ray_trainer.py`, `trainer_base.py`, `workers/engine/utils.py`, `workers/config/engine.py` and its generated yaml), not in any attention or engine code.
- [x] Title format `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`

### Test

We test packed-equals-unpacked by two independent routes, so the oracle and the production path do not share an attention implementation.

CPU, exact (`cpu_unit_tests.yml` picks up the `_on_cpu.py` files; the two `tests/utils` files run in `gpu_unit_tests.yml`):
```bash
pytest tests/workers/test_prefix_packing_on_cpu.py tests/workers/test_prefix_packing_engine_on_cpu.py \
  tests/utils/test_prepare_micro_batches_with_group_size.py tests/utils/test_seqlen_balancing.py
```
We run a tiny fp32 Qwen2 through SDPA with a hand-built dense tree mask, which we first check against a brute-force per-sample forward, and require packed log-probs, entropy, values and every parameter gradient to match at `atol=1e-5`. We also unit-test pack/unpack round trips, label alignment, group-detection edge cases, tail padding, the nothing-shared fallback, every rejection check, the layer guard (including across FSDP's kwarg copy) and micro-batch grouping.

GPU (added to `model.yml` next to `test_transformer.py`), H100, flash-attn 2.8.3, transformers 5.12.1:
```bash
pytest -s tests/models/test_prefix_packing.py   # 14 passed
```
We compare the production path (bf16, varlen flash-attention, the packed wrapper) against the existing rmpad forward: Qwen2 (with and without sliding window) and Qwen3, fused kernels on/off, gradient checkpointing on/off, plus the critic, plus an sdpa model that must leave the layer counter at zero. Log-probs and entropy match within `atol=1e-2`, gradient cosine > 0.999.

End-to-end GRPO, Qwen3-4B, 2x H100, FSDP + vLLM, `rollout.n=8`, 128 prompts/step, 20 steps, mean of steps 5-20, the flag the only difference:

| | 2k-token prompt: baseline | packed | speedup | GSM8K (83-token prompt): baseline | packed | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `timing_s/old_log_prob` | 44.8 s | 14.3 s | 3.13x | 15.8 s | 13.3 s | 1.19x |
| `timing_s/ref` | 60.5 s | 15.6 s | 3.88x | 17.1 s | 11.1 s | 1.54x |
| `timing_s/update_actor` | 158.4 s | 51.2 s | 3.09x | 69.2 s | 59.3 s | 1.17x |
| `timing_s/step` | 289.5 s | 107.1 s | **2.70x** | 123.0 s | 104.4 s | **1.18x** |
| `prefix_packing_token_ratio` | | 3.65 | | | 1.10 | |

With the long prompt the actor phases reach ~85% of the 3.65x token saving and the ref exceeds it. On GSM8K every phase beats the 1.10x token saving (1.18x on the step), because dynamic batching now budgets by packed length and runs fewer, fuller micro-batches; the token ratio is a floor on the speedup, not an estimate of it. Rewards match within sampling noise (per-step difference mean -0.003, sd 0.009 with the long prompt; +0.010, sd 0.013 on GSM8K; the binomial standard error of a 1024-sample mean is ~0.01). Peak allocated memory is 38.25 GB per GPU in all four runs, so at this batch size a fixed floor sets the peak and packing neither raises nor lowers it.

Single-GPU forward+backward sweep (Qwen3-4B, fused kernels, gradient checkpointing, 8 x 1024 response tokens): speedup 1.06x at a 64-token prompt, 2.18x at 2048, 3.81x at 8192, at least 84% of the token ratio throughout; peak memory never rises and falls from 35.8 to 18.7 GB at 8192, so the same GPU holds roughly twice the response tokens per micro-batch.

### API and Usage Example

```bash
actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.use_prefix_packing=True   # ref follows the actor
critic.fsdp.use_prefix_packing=True
```
Off by default; a user who does not set it runs today's code. If the dead `use_prefix_grouper` flag is also set, prefix packing wins (`balance_batch` follows the packing grouping); we remove that flag in a follow-up. We check at model build that `use_remove_padding=True`, `ulysses_sequence_parallel_size=1`, `flash_attention_2`/`3` on CUDA with flash-attn >= 2.1, a text-only model, and not a model that takes `cu_seqlens` directly (linear-attention hybrids), and we reject top-k distillation, score centering, router replay and multi-modal inputs per micro-batch, each with an explicit error.

### Design & Code Changes

- `verl/workers/utils/prefix_packing.py` (new): group detection by prompt token ids (exact by construction, no `uid` needed), the pack/unpack plan, budget helpers, the support checks and the layer counter.
- `verl/workers/engine/fsdp/transformer_impl.py`: pack in `prepare_model_inputs`, unpack in `prepare_model_outputs` (actor and critic); run plain rmpad when a micro-batch shares nothing; raise if any attention layer bypassed the packed path; log `prefix_packing_token_ratio`.
- `verl/models/transformers/monkey_patch.py`, `dense_common.py`: the flash-attention wrapper handles the `prefix_packing` kwarg (gather K/V, explicit `cu_seqlens`, record the layer); the fused-kernel forward passes it on.
- `verl/utils/seqlen_balancing.py`, `verl/workers/engine/utils.py`: dynamic batching keeps same-prompt samples in one micro-batch, budgeted by packed length, and splits a group over budget with its own trunk per part.
- `verl/trainer/ppo/ray_trainer.py`, `v1/trainer_base.py`, `trainer/ppo/utils.py`: with the flag on, `balance_batch` keeps each prompt's samples on one rank.
- `verl/workers/utils/padding.py`: `get_prompt_lens` shared with the packer.
- Config field (`workers/config/engine.py`, yaml), docs (`docs/perf/perf_tuning.rst`, `docs/examples/config.rst`), example toggle in `run_qwen3_4b_fsdp.sh`, CI step in `model.yml`.

Follow-ups, not in this PR: linear-attention hybrids (recurrent-state handoff at the trunk inside the existing `qwen3_5.py` packed-sequence patch), Ulysses SP, sharing beyond the prompt for multi-turn trees, removing the dead PrefixGrouper code.

I developed this PR myself and used AI assistance for code review, test design and this write-up. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

- [x] Tests added to CI.
- [x] CI requested in the `ci-request` Slack channel.

+def _make_batch(spec, vocab: int = 97, seed: int = 0):
+    """``spec`` is a list of ``(n, prompt_len, resp_lens)``, one entry per shared prompt."""
+    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
+    rows, prompt_lens, resp_lens = [], [], []

+            prompt_lens.append(p)
+            resp_lens.append(r)
+    return rows, torch.tensor(prompt_lens, dtype=torch.int64), resp_lens

+def _dense_tree_mask(meta: PrefixPackingAttnMeta) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Boolean ``(num_rows, num_rows)`` mask with bottom-right causal alignment per segment."""
+    mask = torch.zeros(meta.num_rows, meta.num_rows, dtype=torch.bool)
+    cu_q, cu_k = meta.cu_seqlens_q.tolist(), meta.cu_seqlens_k.tolist()
+    for s in range(len(cu_q) - 1):
+        keys = meta.kv_index[cu_k[s] : cu_k[s + 1]]
+        num_q, num_k = cu_q[s + 1] - cu_q[s], cu_k[s + 1] - cu_k[s]
+        for i in range(num_q):

+"""Shared-prefix packing for the no-padding micro-batch layout.
+
+Adjacent samples with an identical prompt are packed as one trunk plus one branch per sample::
+
+    [prompt[:-1]] [prompt[-1] + response_1] ... [prompt[-1] + response_n]
+
+Each branch repeats the last prompt token because ``no_padding_2_padding`` reads the first
+response log-prob from that row. A branch attends to ``[trunk; branch]`` through one varlen
+flash-attention call, so the result equals the unpacked forward.
+"""

+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field, replace
+
+import torch
+from tensordict import TensorDict
+from transformers import PretrainedConfig
+from transformers.modeling_flash_attention_utils import flash_attn_supports_top_left_mask
+
+from verl.utils.device import is_cuda_available
+from verl.utils.model import extract_multi_modal_inputs
+

+    "PrefixPackingAttnMeta",
+    "PrefixPackingPlan",
+    "find_prefix_groups",
+    "build_prefix_packing_plan",
+    "packed_group_lens",
+    "split_groups_to_budget",
+    "check_prefix_packing_supported",
+    "check_prefix_packing_micro_batch",
+    "check_layers_seen",
+]
+
+
+class _LayerCounter:
+    # A plain object, not a dataclass field value: FSDP copies dataclass kwargs with
+    # ``dataclasses.replace`` when moving them to the device, and the copy must share the count.
+    __slots__ = ("value",)
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self.value = 0
+
+
+@dataclass
+class PrefixPackingAttnMeta:
+    """Attention metadata of one packed micro-batch, passed to the attention wrapper as a kwarg.
+
+    Args:
+        kv_index: ``(total_k,)`` packed-row ids; segment ``s`` attends to
+            ``kv_index[cu_seqlens_k[s]:cu_seqlens_k[s + 1]]``.
+        cu_seqlens_q: ``(num_segments + 1,)`` int32 cumulative query lengths.
+        cu_seqlens_k: ``(num_segments + 1,)`` int32 cumulative key lengths.
+        max_seqlen_q: Longest query segment.
+        max_seqlen_k: Longest key segment.
+        num_rows: Packed rows, including any tail pad.
+    """
+
+    kv_index: torch.Tensor
+    cu_seqlens_q: torch.Tensor
+    cu_seqlens_k: torch.Tensor
+    max_seqlen_q: int
+    max_seqlen_k: int
+    num_rows: int
+    counter: _LayerCounter = field(default_factory=_LayerCounter, repr=False, compare=False)
+
+    @property
+    def layers_seen(self) -> int:
+        """Number of attention layers that took the packed path in the last forward."""
+        return self.counter.value
+
+    def record_layer(self) -> None:
+        """Count one attention layer; called by the attention wrapper."""
+        self.counter.value += 1
+
+    def with_tail_pad(self, pad_size: int) -> PrefixPackingAttnMeta:
+        """Return a copy with ``pad_size`` trailing rows that attend only to themselves."""
+        if pad_size <= 0:
+            return self
+        pad_rows = torch.arange(self.num_rows, self.num_rows + pad_size, device=self.kv_index.device)
+        return replace(
+            self,
+            kv_index=torch.cat([self.kv_index, pad_rows]),
+            cu_seqlens_q=torch.cat([self.cu_seqlens_q, self.cu_seqlens_q[-1:] + pad_size]),
+            cu_seqlens_k=torch.cat([self.cu_seqlens_k, self.cu_seqlens_k[-1:] + pad_size]),
+            max_seqlen_q=max(self.max_seqlen_q, pad_size),
+            max_seqlen_k=max(self.max_seqlen_k, pad_size),
+            num_rows=self.num_rows + pad_size,
+            counter=_LayerCounter(),

+class PrefixPackingPlan:
+    """Pack and unpack indices of one micro-batch.
+
+    Args:
+        attn: Attention metadata of the packed rows.
+        pack_index: ``packed = flat[pack_index]`` for ids, positions and temperature.
+        unpack_index: ``unpacked = packed_output[unpack_index]`` for per-token outputs.
+        num_unpacked: Tokens before packing.
+        num_packed: Tokens after packing.
+    """
+
+    attn: PrefixPackingAttnMeta
+    pack_index: torch.Tensor
+    unpack_index: torch.Tensor
+    num_unpacked: int
+    num_packed: int
+
+
+def find_prefix_groups(input_ids: torch.Tensor, prompt_lens: torch.Tensor) -> tuple[list[int], list[int], list[int]]:
+    """Group adjacent samples whose prompts are identical.
+
+    Samples are never reordered. A prompt shorter than two tokens is never shared.
+
+    Args:
+        input_ids: Jagged nested tensor of token ids.
+        prompt_lens: ``(batch,)`` prompt lengths.
+
+    Returns:
+        ``(group_sizes, seq_lens, prompt_lens)`` as Python lists.
+    """
+    flat = input_ids.values()
+    offsets = input_ids.offsets().to(torch.int64)
+    batch_size = prompt_lens.numel()
+    prompt_lens = prompt_lens.to(device=flat.device, dtype=torch.int64)
+    host = torch.cat([offsets, prompt_lens]).tolist()
+    offsets_l, prompt_lens_l = host[: batch_size + 1], host[batch_size + 1 :]
+    seq_lens_l = [end - start for start, end in zip(offsets_l[:-1], offsets_l[1:], strict=True)]
+    assert all(p <= s for p, s in zip(prompt_lens_l, seq_lens_l, strict=True)), "prompt longer than sample"
+    if batch_size == 0:
+        return [], seq_lens_l, prompt_lens_l
+
+    max_prompt = max(prompt_lens_l)
+    if batch_size > 1 and max_prompt >= 2:
+        pos = torch.arange(max_prompt, device=flat.device)
+        toks = flat[(offsets[:-1, None] + pos).clamp_(max=flat.numel() - 1)]
+        in_prompt = pos < prompt_lens[:, None]
+        same_toks = ((toks[1:] == toks[:-1]) | ~in_prompt[1:]).all(dim=-1)
+        joinable = ((prompt_lens[1:] == prompt_lens[:-1]) & same_toks & (prompt_lens[1:] >= 2)).tolist()
+    else:
+        joinable = [False] * (batch_size - 1)
+
+    group_sizes = [1]
+    for join in joinable:
+        if join:
+            group_sizes[-1] += 1
+        else:
+            group_sizes.append(1)
+    return group_sizes, seq_lens_l, prompt_lens_l
+
+
+def build_prefix_packing_plan(input_ids: torch.Tensor, prompt_lens: torch.Tensor) -> PrefixPackingPlan:
+    """Build the packing plan of one micro-batch.
+
+    Args:
+        input_ids: Jagged nested tensor of token ids.
+        prompt_lens: ``(batch,)`` prompt lengths.
+
+    Returns:
+        The plan. Without any shared prompt it reproduces the unpacked layout.
+    """
+    device = input_ids.offsets().device
+    group_sizes, seq_lens, prompt_lens_l = find_prefix_groups(input_ids, prompt_lens)
+    offsets = [0]
+    for length in seq_lens:
+        offsets.append(offsets[-1] + length)
+
+    pack, unpack, kv, q_lens, k_lens = [], [], [], [], []
+    cursor = 0
+
+    def add_segment(src_start: int, length: int, keys_before: list[torch.Tensor]) -> torch.Tensor:
+        nonlocal cursor
+        rows = torch.arange(cursor, cursor + length)
+        pack.append(torch.arange(src_start, src_start + length))
+        kv.extend([*keys_before, rows])
+        q_lens.append(length)
+        k_lens.append(length + sum(k.numel() for k in keys_before))
+        cursor += length
+        return rows
+
+    row = 0
+    for size in group_sizes:
+        trunk_len = prompt_lens_l[row] - 1 if size > 1 else 0
+        trunk = add_segment(offsets[row], trunk_len, []) if trunk_len else None
+        for sample in range(row, row + size):
+            keys_before = [trunk] if trunk is not None else []
+            branch = add_segment(offsets[sample] + trunk_len, seq_lens[sample] - trunk_len, keys_before)
+            unpack.extend([*keys_before, branch])
+        row += size
+
+    def cat(chunks: list[torch.Tensor]) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return torch.cat(chunks).to(device) if chunks else torch.empty(0, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
+
+    attn = PrefixPackingAttnMeta(
+        kv_index=cat(kv),
+        cu_seqlens_q=torch.tensor([0] + q_lens).cumsum(0).to(device=device, dtype=torch.int32),
+        cu_seqlens_k=torch.tensor([0] + k_lens).cumsum(0).to(device=device, dtype=torch.int32),
+        max_seqlen_q=max(q_lens, default=0),
+        max_seqlen_k=max(k_lens, default=0),
+        num_rows=cursor,
+    )
+    return PrefixPackingPlan(
+        attn=attn, pack_index=cat(pack), unpack_index=cat(unpack), num_unpacked=offsets[-1], num_packed=cursor
+    )
+

+def packed_group_lens(group_sizes: list[int], seq_lens: list[int], prompt_lens: list[int]) -> list[int]:
+    """Token count of each group after packing.
+
+    Args:
+        group_sizes: Group sizes in batch order.
+        seq_lens: Per-sample sequence lengths.
+        prompt_lens: Per-sample prompt lengths.
+
+    Returns:
+        One packed length per group.
+    """
+    lens, row = [], 0
+    for size in group_sizes:
+        total = sum(seq_lens[row : row + size])
+        lens.append(total - (size - 1) * (prompt_lens[row] - 1) if size > 1 else total)
+        row += size
+    return lens

+def split_groups_to_budget(
+    group_sizes: list[int], seq_lens: list[int], prompt_lens: list[int], max_token_len: int
+) -> list[int]:
+    """Split groups whose packed length exceeds ``max_token_len``; each part keeps its own trunk.
+
+    Args:
+        group_sizes: Group sizes in batch order.
+        seq_lens: Per-sample sequence lengths.
+        prompt_lens: Per-sample prompt lengths.
+        max_token_len: Token budget of one micro-batch.
+
+    Returns:
+        Group sizes in batch order, with the same total.
+    """
+    out, row = [], 0
+    for size in group_sizes:
+        trunk_len = prompt_lens[row] - 1
+        count, length = 0, trunk_len
+        for sample in range(row, row + size):
+            branch_len = seq_lens[sample] - trunk_len
+            if count and length + branch_len > max_token_len:
+                out.append(count)
+                count, length = 0, trunk_len
+            count += 1
+            length += branch_len
+        out.append(count)
+        row += size
+    return out

+    """Raise if ``use_prefix_packing=True`` cannot work with this model and engine setup.

+    Args:

+        pass_packed_cu_seqlens: Whether the model takes ``cu_seqlens`` directly.

+    Raises:

+    problems = []
+    if not use_remove_padding:
+        problems.append("use_remove_padding=False (packing works on the no-padding path)")
+    if ulysses_sp_size > 1:
+        problems.append("Ulysses sequence parallelism")
+    attn_impl = getattr(config, "_attn_implementation", None)
